en.name: Miguel Pro
en.summary: Mexican Jesuit executed during the anti-Catholic Cristero persecution, famously photographed with arms outstretched in a cross shape moments before his death.
en.body: Miguel Pro was a Mexican Jesuit ordained abroad during a period when the Mexican government's anti-clerical laws had made priestly ministry effectively illegal at home, and he returned to Mexico City anyway to minister secretly to the underground Catholic community, adopting a series of disguises, businessman, mechanic, even at times posing as a police officer, to move through the city administering sacraments while evading the authorities. He was arrested on a fabricated charge of involvement in an assassination attempt against a former president, a charge historians generally regard as unfounded, and President Plutarco Elias Calles, seeking to make an example, ordered his execution by firing squad without trial in 1927. Pro faced the firing squad calmly, forgave his executioners aloud, and stretched his arms out in the shape of a cross as the shots were fired, a moment captured in newspaper photographs that were widely published and became a powerful and enduring image of the Cristero-era persecution of the Mexican Church. He was beatified by Pope John Paul II in 1988, and his cause for full canonization continues.
